gen-gf-happy-monkey-crimson-pro: Happy Monkey draws every line like it was traced along a ruler, with a bold, slightly cheeky look. Crimson Pro is the classic serif underneath, its strokes swelling and thinning softly where the heading never bothers to.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-fs-neco: Distinctive from the first glance, Happy Monkey bends its letters like neon tubing, every stroke the same thickness. And Neco, a classic serif, swells gently along its curves, so the pair's real strength is how firmly they disagree.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-fs-recia: Recia is a classic serif with a light modulation you only notice up close, its diagonals pressed a touch thinner than its verticals. But Happy Monkey's rolling-ball-pen line is the louder voice, and that gap in temperament is what makes the pair.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-alegreya: Bookish at heart, Alegreya sits below a heading where every stroke ends at the same measured thickness. Alegreya, with its soft accents of heavier strokes, brings a reading rhythm that Happy Monkey simply doesn't have, and that is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-alike-angular: Wide gaps in the e and a line that looks ballpoint-drawn make Happy Monkey instantly recognizable. Alike Angular answers with serif stems just slightly thicker than their connecting strokes, and that mild texture against the heading's flat line is the pair's best trick.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-alyamama: Happy Monkey has no thick and thin parts in any letter, so it stays bold and uniform from end to end. But Alyamama, a classic serif, keeps a modest gap between stems and hairlines, which is what the heading can't do.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-ancizar-serif: Tails and terminals as thick as the main stems give Happy Monkey a chunky, drawn-by-one-pen character. Ancizar Serif reads like lightly engraved brass, low-key in contrast and gaping wide, so a long passage would feel quietly bookish.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-andada-pro: Traditional in spirit, Andada Pro sets its thick and thin strokes close enough to feel related, under a heading drawn as if with a ballpoint. Happy Monkey carries the swagger while the serif lets the eye move easily.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-aref-ruqaa: Happy Monkey makes its tails and terminals as thick as the main stems, giving a bold, ruler-straight look up top. Aref Ruqaa, a classic serif with open bowls, suits a body a bit larger than usual.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-aref-ruqaa-ink: Classic and literary, Aref Ruqaa Ink takes over below a heading whose curves are as heavy as its stems, like cord. Aref Ruqaa Ink swings mellowly from thick to thin, so a long passage would feel warm and unhurried.
